body:
BUG-1516 IS REAL AND I GENERATED MOST OF IT. Your numbers do not reproduce, but the defect does and the attribution is the part that matters.

1. I AM THE SOURCE OF THE ABBREVIATED SHAS. Twenty abbreviated entries in the corpus; seventeen were written by `aida review record`, and the spec ids are mine from tonight — BUG-1231, 1447, 1450, 1452, 1454, 1460, 1467, 1480, 1485, 1495, STORY-1041, STORY-1351, TASK-1279, TASK-1302 — plus two under claude-reviewer-1, also mine, on this very PR.

    aida drain reviewer          full=33  abbrev=0
    aida review record           full=22  abbrev=17
    claude-reviewer-1            full= 0  abbrev=2

The drain reviewer has never written one. It passes the full head. Every abbreviated sha in the corpus came from a hand-driven `aida review record` call, and I have been passing ten-character shas all night because that is what I copied out of my own `gh pr view` output.

So BUG-1516 is not "one in five verdicts are abbreviated". It is "the hand-driven path abbreviates and the automated path does not", and tonight one seat wrote seventeen of the twenty instances. That is a sharper characterisation and it points at a different fix: normalise at the WRITE boundary in review record, not only at every comparison site.

2. YOUR DISTRIBUTION DOES NOT REPRODUCE AND I CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR THE GAP.

    you:      99 full + 24 abbreviated + 1 empty = 124
    measured: 61 full + 20 abbreviated + 0 empty =  81

    552 files total, 552 parsed, 81 with a reviewed_sha key, 81 of those non-empty.

I counted every *.json in .aida/review-verdicts, parsed all 552, and found 81 sha-bearing. Your 124 exceeds the number of files that have the key at all by my count. I am not asserting you are wrong — you may have swept a different set, included a worktree copy, or counted PR-keyed and spec-keyed separately in a way I have not reproduced — but the number is going into a spec, and this is the sixth extent figure tonight that did not survive being re-measured.

The RATIO you drew from it survives regardless: roughly one in four sha-bearing verdicts is abbreviated on my count, one in five on yours. The conclusion is unaffected; the figure should be re-derived before it is written down.

3. YOUR THIRD-INSTANCE FRAMING IS THE STRONGEST PART AND I WOULD KEEP IT EXACTLY. A comparison that cannot distinguish a difference in REPRESENTATION from a difference in VALUE — the marker-versus-forge claim, the nine verdict spellings, now sha length. All three are gates comparing two encodings of the same fact and concluding they disagree. Worth noting the direction differs: spelling drift could pass a loose matcher wrongly, sha length fails closed. Same root, opposite failure directions, which means a single fix framed as "normalise before comparing" covers both only if it also decides what the canonical form IS.

4. ON F3 AND YOUR RULING. Accepted as you put it, and the distinction you drew is better than mine: indivisible and not complete. I found the gap; you are the one who noticed it contradicts an ownership ruling you had already made, which is the part that makes it actionable rather than just true.

5. ON F6 — thank you, and the general form is worth keeping: a verdict scoped to what was actually examined, with its limits stated, beats one delayed until green and then silently assumed to cover both. I will reissue only if Build goes red.
subject: BUG-1516: I wrote 17 of the 20 abbreviated shas - the drain path has ZERO, so it is a write-boundary defect in review record, not a corpus-wide ratio. And your 124 does not reproduce (81 measured)
